title: Anyone using Geminis for game development in here?
author: Patient-Software-168
selftext:
I am looking for a new home because codex is unusable after all the nerfs. 

  
I tried the free test of Gemini hydrogen and I was really surprised. 

  
It made a better version of a test fps on free hydrogen than my all on chatgpt. 

The only problem is the performance of the game which wasn't the best, but I guess that could be optimized. 

  
Wanted to hear about peoples experience with Google Gemini, because sadly I cannot find much info about it. It doesn't seem to be as popular as the competitors. 

  
And was wondering if people have tried Gemini with complex games and if they had any succes with it.

comments.author: Electrical-Local-814
comments.body: Opus is the standard from what I've seen. I've only ever had issues with gemini.

replies.author: joeyb908
replies.body: Gemini 4 Neon’s code output is pretty much equivalent to Opus 5.5, but Opus 5.5 is still king when it comes to anything that’s going to be using shaders or visual design.

replies.author: Patient-Software-168
replies.body: But isn't neon very expensive compared to opus

replies.author: joeyb908
replies.body:
If you have the subscription plan, use Hydrogen Medium to scout the repo, have Neon Medium/High to implement.

It’s good to have cross-family models check each other’s work every now and then anyways for bugs or optimization. Game dev isn’t as big of an issue as other professions since we can usually immediately see the implementation and the bugs.

replies.author: Recoil42
replies.body: Gemini Neon is equivalent or better now.

replies.author: Electrical-Local-814
replies.body: How is usage on the $20/mo plan?

replies.author: Recoil42
replies.body:
I'd peg it at less usage than Opus 5.5 on the Claude $20/mo plan, but with a model that acts more like Fable 5.2 in a lot of instances. (It's worse than Opus at design, but utterly spectacular hill-climbing really hard engineering tasks so far.) 

When you take into account it also gives you a bunch of extras like 5TB of Google Drive, Youtube Premium, and Flow credits, it's kind of a no-brainer. There's a half-off annual plan going around right now too for Black Friday.

replies.author: Electrical-Local-814
replies.body: I'm making a really complex simulation game so I may try it.

comments.author: acexprt
comments.body: I think Gemini is amazing for HTML browser games. It really was ahead of Claud, grok and chat GPT earlier this year. I don’t think that’s the case anymore.

replies.body: It will pop up when it's black Friday. I don't know which time exactly.

replies.author: Recoil42

comments.author: Ferniclestix
comments.body: Imo, gemini is good for concepting, individual prompting small things. Claude by comparison is much better at larger projects and its less forgetful, gemini will forget features if you are using the web interface and just getting one big code dump

comments.author: jimbojohndoe
comments.body:
I been using it trial out some 3d Unity games and cut scenes. Does the job well, and in terms of reviewing/playing/feedback, I think it does the best. I use Fable and Astra regularly, and I personally felt Gemini Carbon did best for me to review my game for oversights, game play specific, and coherence. I used it on my 3d Godot project I made with Claude, and it does quite well in optimizing my game, so I do feel that is a big plus.

I don't think its best in creativity on art, but so far its pretty cool I think. The tasks on Gemini Neon does hang up more regularly than any other provider for me, so that is about the constant issue I have right now.

comments.author: TheVoyant
comments.body: Its good, Neon Xhigh or Carbon High, not great for visuals or UI but the rest is solid

comments.body: They allow shitty small context window in AGY (like, 256k or 384k), so completely unusable for any large game. Only small PoC
